author: /root/transport_dependency_audit
head: 4c4b565056cbcaff1151e0ba98a4feb455b45d72
scope: Standalone SPI ordinary deferred response and late SSE ownership tests; no production implementation or full HTTP routing/transport conformance claim

findings.problem: The new late eventStream path is exercised only with a successful drain. It does not prove ownership cleanup when the adapter-owned drain throws after initial service return and promotion to SSE.
findings.why_existing_checks_are_insufficient: A successful late drain and an ordinary-client write failure do not execute the late-SSE error path. Existing pre-return SSE error tests cannot establish that promotion leaves no duplicate AsyncContext ownership or stream slot after a failing late drain.
findings.required_test: After observing the initial service return and pending client, register a late StreamDrain that writes or throws IOException/RuntimeException. Assert the error/abort outcome, abort callback count, exactly one AsyncContext completion, zero inFlight/pool ownership, and rejection of later finish/commit resurrection. Cover both checked and unchecked drain failures where adapter code has distinct catch paths.

findings.problem: The late-stream capacity test observes one occupied SSE slot but never attempts another late SSE registration while that configured single slot remains occupied.
findings.why_existing_checks_are_insufficient: The new ordinary-to-SSE promotion could bypass or mishandle stream admission rejection while still passing all successful one-slot assertions. Earlier synchronous SSE limit tests do not exercise late promotion rejection.
findings.required_test: Keep one late SSE drain blocked with a latch, then convert a second already-returned pending ordinary exchange into an SSE. Assert the existing configured rejection outcome/abort callback and exactly-once cleanup for that rejected exchange, while the first stream remains live and owns exactly one slot. Release the first stream, verify both requests terminate without leaked inflight/slots, and prove later ordinary admission remains usable.

checks_passed: Actual Jetty/Servlet requests demonstrate pending ownership after service return rather than mocking only AsyncListener callbacks
Delayed text/JSON byte streams, synchronous unsupported-async baseline, timeout, client reset, graceful stop, deadline abort, unsupported configuration and finish/abort race have concrete assertions
Tests observe response bytes, inFlight, SSE pool occupancy and complete() call counts rather than only waiting for no exception
Executors/latches have cleanup and bounded waits
Current suite fails before implementation; no ignored/expected-failure test is being claimed as completed feature evidence
Dependencies and SPI remain unchanged in the reviewed test commit
Full core-routing integration and raw URI matrix remain explicitly outside this foundation's completion claim
suggestions_not_blocking: Record forced before-return and after-return completion schedules if the implementation introduces a distinct ownership transfer window; existing manual after-return and synchronous-before-return cases already establish endpoints, while the30-iteration race provides stress coverage
next: Author adds the missing negative late-SSE cases, then host requests round2. Maximum3 rounds; stop on first PASS.
